{{further|2026 Rolex Shanghai Masters}}

[[Alejandro Davidovich Fokina]] defeated [[Rafael Jódar]] in the final, 1–6, 7–6<sup>(7–5)</sup>, 6–4 to win the singles tennis title at the [[2026 Rolex Shanghai Masters|2026 Shanghai Masters]]. He saved a match point (in the third round against [[Frances Tiafoe]]) en route to his first [[ATP Masters 1000]] title and third career [[ATP Tour]] title.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alejandro Davidovich Fokina beats Rafael Jodar to win Shanghai Masters for his biggest career title |url=https://apnews.com/article/shanghai-masters-tennis-jodar-davidovich-fokina-b7528232e022bfd8717cb0c66e240c2b |website=Associated Press |access-date=18 October 2026 |date=18 October 2026}}</ref>

[[Valentin Vacherot]] was the defending champion,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/tennis/story/_/id/46570136/valentin-vacherot-beats-cousin-arthur-rinderknech-win-shanghai-masters|title=Valentin Vacherot beats cousin Arthur Rinderknech to win Shanghai Masters|publisher=ESPN|accessdate=12 October 2025}}</ref> but lost in the third round to [[Tommy Paul (tennis)|Tommy Paul]].<ref>{{Cite web | last = Pagliaro | first = Richard | title = Paul Dethrones Defending Champion Vacherot in Shanghai Sweep | publisher = Tennis Now | date = 2026-10-12 | url = https://tennisnow.com/paul-dethrones-defending-champion-vacherot-in-shanghai-sweep/ | accessdate = 2026-10-12}}</ref>

With the absence of [[Jannik Sinner]] since [[2026 Wimbledon Championships – Men's singles|Wimbledon]] due to an ongoing knee injury and [[Carlos Alcaraz]]'s third-round defeat, [[Alexander Zverev]] clinched the [[List of ATP number 1 ranked singles tennis players#Year-end No. 1 players|year-end No. 1 ranking]] for the first time in his career by reaching the fourth round, becoming the first German and 20th player overall to do so in singles.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/alexander-zverev-clinches-year-end-no-1-2026|title=Zverev clinches ATP Year-End No. 1 presented by PIF honours spot|website=atptour.com|date=12 October 2026}}</ref> 

Aged 20 years and 29 days old, Jódar became the youngest [[Shanghai Masters (tennis)|Shanghai]] finalist since the tournament's inception in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.atptour.com/en/news/medvedev-jodar-shanghai-2026-saturday|title=Jodar storms to first Masters 1000 final in Shanghai|website=ATPTour.com|accessdate=17 October 2026}}</ref>
